beats.narration_text: Hallo. This is Liam, in for Bear. Claude just opened a portal for plugins. So the question isn't only how you build one. It's how you get one live.

show.event: backspaces 'build one' → 'get one live' on the spoken correction

props.text:
What is a Claude plugin,
and how do I build one?

beats.motion_claim: The writer types the naive build question and corrects it to the real one: getting a plugin live.

qc.sparse_reason: Hesitant-writer bookend: the correction is the motion.

beats.narration_text: Three terms. MCP, the Model Context Protocol: an open standard that plugs Claude into outside tools and data. A skill: written instructions Claude loads to do one kind of task well. And a plugin: a package that carries MCP connectors, skills, or both.

terms.meaning: Model Context Protocol — an open standard that plugs Claude into outside tools and data

a package that carries MCP connectors, skills, or both

beats.narration_text: Start with the plugin itself. Picture it as a sealed box. What goes inside?

shot.motion_claim: A sealed cardboard box with terracotta tape drops onto the stage and settles; the word 'plugin' under it.

beats.narration_text: A plugin is a package. Inside go MCP connectors, which plug Claude into outside tools and data, and skills, which are written instructions Claude can follow. A plugin can carry either one, or both.

shot.visual_intent: The lid lifts off; two dark MCP blocks rise out to the left and two skill pages to the right, each labelled once.

beats.narration_text: There are two ways to submit one. Way one is a single MCP connector. You point it at your own remote MCP server, and that's the submission.

shot.visual_intent: One MCP block on the left; a cable draws from its port to a server stack on the right, whose lights come on.
shot.motion_claim: One MCP block on the left; a cable draws from its port to a server stack on the right, whose lights come on.

beats.narration_text: Way two is a plugin bundle. You put your MCP servers and your skills together in a GitHub repository, and you submit the repo.

shot.visual_intent: An open box; an MCP block and two skill pages drop into it; a folder tag 'GitHub repo' clips onto the box.
shot.motion_claim: An open box; an MCP block and two skill pages drop into it; a folder tag 'GitHub repo' clips onto the box.

beats.narration_text: You submit right inside Claude, from the directory's manage page, if you're a developer on a paid plan. The moment you hit submit, the plugin is checked and safety-scanned, so problems show up early.

shot.visual_intent: A Claude window with a Submit button; a cursor clicks it; a scan beam sweeps the plugin box and a shield with a check appears.
shot.motion_claim: A Claude window with a Submit button; a cursor clicks it; a scan beam sweeps the plugin box and a shield with a check appears.

beats.narration_text: Then you can track it. The portal shows where your plugin is in review, what the safety scan found, and any changes it recommends. Submitted. In review. Live.

shot.visual_intent: An isometric conveyor with three gates labelled Submit, In review, Live; the box rides through each gate and each turns terracotta with a check.

beats.narration_text: Once it's live, you can see it being used: installs by product and version, how often your listing gets viewed, and which searches lead people to it.

beats.narration_text: Why does this matter now? Claude's developer team says MCP usage across Claude products is up a hundred and ten times this year, and that plugins are becoming the way to build for Claude.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude: I use [name a tool] every week. Help me plan a Claude plugin for it: one MCP connector that exposes only the two or three actions I actually need, and one skill that says when and how to use them well. List what the connector needs access to, and flag anything it should not expose. Don't write code yet. Then check two things yourself. Does every action trace to something you actually do with that tool? And does the connector reach anything the job doesn't need? If it does, cut it before you submit.
